content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a short essay on creation. Your essay should include the importance of creation and measures to be taken to encourage creation. You are required to write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

modelEssay.title: The Significance of Creation
modelEssay.content:
Creation is the engine of progress and the cornerstone of innovation. It propels society forward and fosters a culture of continuous improvement. In today's rapidly evolving world, the importance of creation cannot be overstated.

Firstly, creation is vital for economic growth. It leads to the development of new products and services, which in turn stimulates the market and generates employment opportunities. Moreover, creative industries are often at the forefront of technological advancements, driving innovation and competitiveness.

Secondly, measures to encourage creation are essential. Education systems should prioritize nurturing creativity in students from an early age. Additionally, governments can provide incentives for businesses to invest in research and development, thus fostering an environment conducive to innovation.

In conclusion, creation is not just a buzzword but a driving force behind societal advancement. By recognizing its importance and taking appropriate measures, we can ensure a prosperous and innovative future.

structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：重申创新的重要性，并提出对未来的展望

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话一。

transcript.text: Guess what?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 猜猜怎么着？

transcript.text: The worst food I ever had was in France.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我吃过的最糟糕的食物是在法国。

transcript.text: Really?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 真的吗？

transcript.text: That's odd.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这很奇怪。

transcript.text: I thought the French were all good cooks.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我以为法国人都是好厨师。

transcript.text: Yes, that's right.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，没错。

transcript.text: I suppose it's really like anywhere else though.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不过我想它其实和其他任何地方一样。

transcript.text: You know, some places are good, some bad.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你知道，有些地方好，有些地方差。

transcript.text: But it's really all our own fault.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但这其实都是我们自己的错。

transcript.text: What do you mean?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你什么意思？

transcript.text: Well, it was the first time I'd been to France.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，那是我第一次去法国。

transcript.text: This was years ago when I was at school.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那是多年前我还在上学的时候。

transcript.text: I went there with my parents' friends from my father's school.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我和父亲的学校里的朋友一起去的。

transcript.text: They'd hired a coach to take them to Switzerland.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们租了一辆大巴车去瑞士。

transcript.text: A school trip?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 学校旅行？

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 对。

transcript.text: Most of them had never been abroad before.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们大多数人以前从未出过国。

transcript.text: We'd crossed the English Channel at night and we set off through France.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们在夜间渡过了英吉利海峡，然后开始穿越法国。

transcript.text: And breakfast time arrived and the coach driver had arranged for us to stop at this little cafe.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 早餐时间到了，大巴车司机安排我们在一家小咖啡馆停下来。

transcript.text: There we all were, tired and hungry, and then we made the great discovery.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们都在那里，又累又饿，然后我们有了重大发现。

transcript.text: What was that?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那是什么？

transcript.text: Bacon and eggs.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 培根和鸡蛋。

transcript.text: Fantastic!
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 太棒了！

transcript.text: The real English breakfast.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 真正的英式早餐。

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的。

transcript.text: Anyway, we didn't know any better.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 总之，我们当时并不知道更好。

transcript.text: So we had it and...
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 于是我们吃了它，然后……

transcript.text: What was it like?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它怎么样？

transcript.text: Disgusting?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 恶心吗？

transcript.text: Oh, it was incredible.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 哦，它太不可思议了。

transcript.text: They just got a bowl and put some fat in it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们只是拿了一个碗，往里面放了一些脂肪。

transcript.text: And then they put some bacon in the fat, broke an egg over the top, and put the whole lot in the oven for about ten minutes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 然后他们把一些培根放在脂肪里，在上面打了一个鸡蛋，把整个东西放进烤箱里大约十分钟。

transcript.text: In the oven?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 在烤箱里？

transcript.text: You're joking.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你在开玩笑吧。

transcript.text: You can't cook bacon and eggs in the oven.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你不能在烤箱里做培根和鸡蛋。

transcript.text: Well, they must have done it that way.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，他们肯定是那样做的。

transcript.text: It was hot, but it wasn't cooked.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 它是热的，但没熟。

transcript.text: There was just this egg floating about in gallons of fat and raw bacon.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 只有这个鸡蛋漂浮在大量的脂肪和生培根中。

transcript.text: Did you actually eat it?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你真的吃了吗？

transcript.text: No, nobody did.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不，没有人。

transcript.text: They all wanted to turn round and go home.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 他们都想转身回家。

transcript.text: You know, back to tea bags and fish and chips.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你知道，回到茶包和炸鱼薯条的生活。

transcript.text: You can't blame them, really.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 真的，你不能责怪他们。

transcript.text: Anyway, the next night we were all given another foreign speciality.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 总之，第二天晚上我们又都得到了另一种外国特色菜。

transcript.text: What was that?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那是什么？

transcript.text: Snails.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 蜗牛。

transcript.text: That really finished them off.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那真的让他们受不了了。

transcript.text: Lovely holiday that was.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那真是个愉快的假期。

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话2。

transcript.text: You say your shop has been doing well.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你说你的商店一直经营得很好。

transcript.text: Could you give me some idea of what doing well means in facts and figures?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你能用事实和数字告诉我“经营得很好”是什么意思吗？

transcript.text: Well, doing well means averaging 1,200 pounds or more a week for about seven years, making almost a quarter of a million pounds.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，“经营得很好”意味着大约七年来，每周平均收入1200英镑或更多，总共赚了近25万英镑。

transcript.text: And doing well means your earnings are rising.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而且“经营得很好”意味着你的收入在上升。

transcript.text: Last year we did slightly over 50,000 and this year we hope to do more than 60,000.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 去年我们收入略超过5万英镑，今年我们希望超过6万英镑。

transcript.text: So that's good if we continue to rise.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以如果我们继续保持增长，那就很好。

transcript.text: Now, that's gross earnings, I assume.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我猜，那是总收入。

transcript.text: What about your expenses?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那你的开支呢？

transcript.text: Yes, that's gross.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，那是总收入。

transcript.text: The expenses, of course, go up steadily.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当然，开支在稳步上升。

transcript.text: And since we've moved to this new shop, the expenses have increased greatly because it's a much bigger shop.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而且自从我们搬到这家新店以来，开支大幅增加，因为这家店大得多。

transcript.text: So I couldn't say exactly what our expenses are.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以我无法确切说出我们的开支是多少。

transcript.text: There's something in the region of six or seven thousand pounds a year, which is not high.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 大约在六七千英镑一年左右，这并不高。

transcript.text: Commercially speaking, it's fairly low and we try to keep our expenses as low as we can.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 从商业角度来看，这相当低，我们尽可能保持开支低。

transcript.text: And your prices are much lower than the same goods in shops round about.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而且你的价格比周围商店的同类商品低得多。

transcript.text: How do the local shopkeepers feel about having a shop doing so well in their midst?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 当地店主对一家商店在他们中间经营得如此之好有什么看法？

transcript.text: Perhaps a lot of them don't realize how well we're doing because we don't make a point of publicizing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 也许他们中的许多人没有意识到我们做得多好，因为我们不特意宣传。

transcript.text: That was a lesson we learned very early on.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这是我们很早就学到的教训。

transcript.text: We were very friendly with all local shopkeepers and we happened to mention to a local shopkeeper how much we had made that week.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们和所有当地店主都很友好，我们碰巧向一位当地店主提到了我们那周赚了多少钱。

transcript.text: He was very unhappy and never as friendly again.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 他非常不高兴，从此再也没有那么友好过。

transcript.text: So we make a point of never publicizing the amount of money we make.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以我们特意从不宣传我们赚了多少钱。

transcript.text: But we're on very good terms with all the shops.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但我们和所有商店关系都很好。

transcript.text: None of them have ever complained that we're putting them out of business or anything like that.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 他们中没有人抱怨我们让他们破产或类似的事情。

transcript.text: I think it's a nice friendly relationship.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我认为这是一种友好和谐的关系。

transcript.text: Maybe if they did know what we made, perhaps they wouldn't be so friendly.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 也许如果他们知道我们赚了多少，他们可能就不会那么友好了。

transcript.text: Passage one.
transcript.translation: 第一篇短文。

transcript.text: Birds are famous for carrying things around.
transcript.translation: 鸟类以四处携带物品而闻名。

transcript.text: Some, like homing pigeons, can be trained to deliver messages and packages.
transcript.translation: 一些鸟类，如信鸽，可以被训练来传递信息和包裹。

transcript.text: Other birds unknowingly carry seeds that cling to them for the ride.
transcript.translation: 其他鸟类则无意中携带附着在它们身上的种子，借此传播。

transcript.text: Canadian scientists have found a worrisome new example of the power that birds have to spread stuff around.
transcript.translation: 加拿大科学家发现了一个令人担忧的新例子，展示了鸟类传播物质的能力。

transcript.text: Way up north in the Canadian Arctic, seabirds are picking up dangerous chemicals in the ocean and delivering them to ponds near where the birds live.
transcript.translation: 在加拿大北极地区的遥远北方，海鸟在海洋中携带危险化学物质，并将它们带到鸟类栖息地附近的池塘中。

transcript.text: Some 10,000 pairs of the birds, called fulmars, a kind of Arctic seabird, make their nests on Devon Island, north of the Arctic Circle.
transcript.translation: 大约10,000对这种名为管鼻鹱的北极海鸟在北极圈以北的德文岛上筑巢。

transcript.text: The fulmars travel some 400 kilometers over the sea to find food.
transcript.translation: 管鼻鹱飞行大约400公里到海上寻找食物。

transcript.text: When they return home, their droppings end up all around their nesting sites, including in nearby ponds.
transcript.translation: 当它们返回家园时，它们的粪便遍布巢穴周围，包括附近的池塘。

transcript.text: Previously, scientists noticed pollutants arriving in the Arctic with the wind.
transcript.translation: 此前，科学家注意到污染物随风传播到北极。

transcript.text: Salmon also carry dangerous chemicals as the fish migrate between rivers and the sea.
transcript.translation: 鲑鱼在河流和海洋之间迁徙时也会携带危险化学物质。

transcript.text: The bodies of fish and other meat-eaters can build up high levels of the chemicals.
transcript.translation: 鱼类和其他肉食动物的体内会积累高水平的化学物质。

transcript.text: To test the polluting power of fulmars, researchers collected samples of deposit from 11 ponds on Devon Island.
transcript.translation: 为了测试管鼻鹱的污染能力，研究人员从德文岛上的11个池塘中采集了沉积物样本。

transcript.text: In ponds closest to the colony, the results showed there were far more pollutants than in ponds less affected by the birds.
transcript.translation: 在最接近鸟群的池塘中，结果显示污染物远远多于受鸟类影响较小的池塘。

transcript.text: The pollutants in the ponds appear to come from fish that fulmars eat when they're out on the ocean.
transcript.translation: 池塘中的污染物似乎来自管鼻鹱在海上捕食的鱼类。

transcript.text: People who live, hunt or fish near bird colonies need to be careful, the researchers say.
transcript.translation: 研究人员表示，居住在鸟群附近、或在附近狩猎或捕鱼的人需要小心。

transcript.text: The birds don't mean to cause harm, but the chemicals they carry can cause major problems.
transcript.translation: 鸟类并非有意造成危害，但它们携带的化学物质可能导致重大问题。

transcript.text: OK, so let's get started.
transcript.translation: 好的，那么我们开始吧。

transcript.text: And to start things off, I think what we need to do is consider a definition.
transcript.translation: 首先，我认为我们需要考虑一个定义。

transcript.text: I'm going to define what love is, but then most of the experiments I'm going to talk about are really focused more on attraction than love.
transcript.translation: 我将定义爱是什么，但接下来我要讨论的大多数实验实际上更关注吸引力而非爱。

transcript.text: And I'm going to pick a definition from a former colleague, Robert Sternberg, who is now the Dean at Tufts University, but was here on our faculty at Yale for nearly 30 years.
transcript.translation: 我将从一位前同事罗伯特·斯滕伯格那里选取一个定义，他现在是塔夫茨大学的院长，但曾在耶鲁大学任教近30年。

transcript.text: And he has a theory of love that argues that it's made up of three components, intimacy, passion and commitment, or what is sometimes called decision commitment.
transcript.translation: 他有一个爱情理论，认为爱情由三个组成部分构成：亲密、激情和承诺，或有时被称为决策承诺。

transcript.text: And these are relatively straightforward.
transcript.translation: 这些相对直接明了。

transcript.text: He argued that you don't have love if you don't have all three of these elements.
transcript.translation: 他认为，如果不具备这三个要素，你就没有爱情。

transcript.text: Intimacy is the feeling of closeness, of connectedness with someone, of bonding.
transcript.translation: 亲密是与某人亲近、联结和依恋的感觉。

transcript.text: Operationally, you could think of intimacy as you share secrets, you share information with this person that you don't share with anybody else.
transcript.translation: 在操作层面，你可以将亲密理解为与这个人分享秘密，分享你不会与其他人分享的信息。

transcript.text: OK, that's really what intimacy is, the bond that comes from sharing information that isn't shared with other people.
transcript.translation: 好的，这就是亲密的本质，即通过分享不与他人分享的信息而形成的纽带。

transcript.text: The second element is passion.
transcript.translation: 第二个要素是激情。

transcript.text: Passion is the drive that leads to romance.
transcript.translation: 激情是导致浪漫的动力。

transcript.text: You can think of it as physical attraction.
transcript.translation: 你可以将其视为身体吸引力。

transcript.text: And Sternberg argues that this is a required component of a love relationship.
transcript.translation: 斯滕伯格认为，这是爱情关系的必要组成部分。

transcript.text: The third element of love in Sternberg's theory is what he calls decision commitment.
transcript.translation: 在斯滕伯格的理论中，爱情的第三个要素是他所称的决策承诺。

transcript.text: The decision that one is in a love relationship, the willingness to label it as such, and a commitment to maintain that relationship, at least for some period of time.
transcript.translation: 决定自己处于一段爱情关系中，愿意将其如此标记，以及维持这段关系的承诺，至少在一定时期内。

transcript.text: Sternberg would argue it's not love if you don't call it love, and if you don't have some desire to maintain the relationship.
transcript.translation: 斯滕伯格会认为，如果你不称之为爱，且没有维持这段关系的愿望，那就不是爱。

transcript.text: So if you have all three of these, intimacy, passion and commitment, in Sternberg's theory you have love.
transcript.translation: 因此，如果你具备所有这三个要素——亲密、激情和承诺，在斯滕伯格的理论中，你就拥有爱情。

transcript.text: Now what's interesting about the theory is what do you have if you only have one out of three, or two out of three?
transcript.translation: 现在，这个理论有趣之处在于，如果你只有三个中的一个或两个，你会拥有什么？

transcript.text: What do you have and how is it different if you have a different two out of three?
transcript.translation: 如果你有三个中不同的两个，你会拥有什么，以及有何不同？

transcript.text: What's interesting about this kind of theorising is it gives rise to many different combinations that can be quite interesting when you break them down and start to look at them carefully.
transcript.translation: 这种理论化的有趣之处在于，它产生了许多不同的组合，当你分解并仔细观察时，这些组合可能相当有趣。

transcript.text: So what I've done is I've taken Sternberg's three elements of love, intimacy, passion and commitment, and I've listed out the different kinds of relationships you would have if you had zero, one, two or three out of the three elements.
transcript.translation: 因此，我所做的就是取斯滕伯格的爱情三要素——亲密、激情和承诺，并列出如果你有零个、一个、两个或三个要素时你会拥有的不同关系类型。

transcript.text: Currently, there's mounting criticism of Michelle Obama's Let's Move campaign, which fights childhood obesity by encouraging youngsters to become more physically active, and has signed on singer Beyonce and basketball player Shaquille O'Neal, both of whom also endorse sodas, which are a major contributor to the obesity epidemic.
transcript.translation: 目前，米歇尔·奥巴马的“让我们动起来”活动受到越来越多的批评，该活动通过鼓励青少年增加身体活动来对抗儿童肥胖症，并且已经签约歌手碧昂斯和篮球运动员沙奎尔·奥尼尔，而他们两人也为苏打饮料代言，这些饮料是肥胖流行病的主要因素。

transcript.text: Now, there's a lot more evidence of how powerful a celebrity, especially a professional athlete, can be in influencing children's behaviour.
transcript.translation: 现在，有更多证据表明名人，尤其是职业运动员，在影响儿童行为方面的力量有多大。

transcript.text: In a report published by the Rudd Centre for Food Policy and Obesity at Yale University, researchers studied 100 professional athletes and their endorsement contracts.
transcript.translation: 在耶鲁大学食品政策与肥胖研究中心发布的一份报告中，研究人员研究了100名职业运动员及其代言合同。

transcript.text: The team focused on athletes, since they are theoretically the best role models for active, healthy lifestyles for children.
transcript.translation: 团队专注于运动员，因为理论上他们是孩子们积极、健康生活方式的最佳榜样。

transcript.text: After sorting the deals by category, they determined that among the 512 brands associated with the athletes, most involved sporting goods, followed closely by food and beverage brands.

transcript.text: Sports drinks, which are often high in sugar and calories, made up most of the food and drink deals, with soft drinks and fast food filling out the remainder.

questionGroups.title: Countries Rush for Upper Hand in Antarctica

material.title: Countries Rush for Upper Hand in Antarctica

paragraphs.text: On a glacier-filled island with fords (峡湾) and elephant seals, Russia has built Antarctica's first Orthodox church on a hill overlooking its research base. Less than an hour away by snowmobile, Chinese laborers have updated the Great Wall Station, a vital part of China's plan to operate five bases on Antarctica, complete with an indoor badminton court and sleeping quarters for 150 people. Not to be outdone, India's futuristic new Bharathi base, built on stilts (柱子) using 134 interlocking shipping containers, resembles a spaceship. Turkey and Iran have announced plans to build bases too.
paragraphs.translation: 在拥有峡湾和象海豹的冰川覆盖岛屿上，俄罗斯在其研究基地上方的小山上建造了南极洲的第一座东正教教堂。乘雪地摩托不到一小时的路程，中国劳工更新了长城站，这是中国计划在南极洲运营五个基地的关键部分，配有室内羽毛球场和可容纳150人的睡眠区。不甘示弱，印度未来主义的新Bharathi基地，建在柱子上，使用134个互锁的集装箱，外观像一艘宇宙飞船。土耳其和伊朗也宣布了建造基地的计划。

paragraphs.text: More than a century has passed since explorers raced to plant their flags at the bottom of the world, and for decades to come this continent is supposed to be protected as a scientific preserve, shielded from intrusions like military activities and mining. But an array of countries are rushing to assert greater influence here, with an eye not just towards the day those protective treaties expire, but also for the strategic and commercial opportunities that already exist.
paragraphs.translation: 一个多世纪以来，探险家们争相在世界底部插旗，未来几十年，这个大陆理应作为科学保护区受到保护，免受军事活动和采矿等入侵。但一系列国家正急于在这里施加更大影响力，不仅着眼于保护条约到期的那一天，也瞄准已经存在的战略和商业机会。

paragraphs.text: The newer players are stepping into what they view as a treasure house of resources. Some of the ventures focus on the Antarctic resources that are already up for grabs, like abundant sea life. South Korea, which operates state-of-the-art bases here, is increasing its fishing of krill (磷虾), found in abundance in the Southern Ocean, while Russia recently frustrated efforts to create one of the world's largest ocean sanctuaries here.
paragraphs.translation: 新玩家正踏入他们视为资源宝库的地方。一些企业专注于已经可以争夺的南极资源，如丰富的海洋生物。韩国在这里运营最先进的基地，正在增加对磷虾的捕捞，磷虾在南大洋大量存在，而俄罗斯最近挫败了在这里建立世界最大海洋保护区之一的努力。

paragraphs.text: Some scientists are examining the potential for harvesting icebergs from Antarctica, which is estimated to have the biggest reserves of fresh water on the planet. Nations are also pressing ahead with space research and satellite projects to expand their global navigation abilities.
paragraphs.translation: 一些科学家正在研究从南极洲开采冰山的潜力，据估计南极洲拥有地球上最大的淡水储备。各国也在推进空间研究和卫星项目，以扩大其全球导航能力。

paragraphs.text: Building on a Soviet-era foothold, Russia is expanding its monitoring stations for Glonass, its version of the Global Positioning System (GPS). At least three Russian stations are already operating in Antarctica -- part of its effort to challenge the dominance of the American GPS, and new stations are planned for sites like than Russian base, in the shadow of the Orthodox Church of the Holy Trinity.
paragraphs.translation: 基于苏联时代的立足点，俄罗斯正在扩大其格洛纳斯（Glonass）监测站，格洛纳斯是俄罗斯版的全球定位系统（GPS）。至少三个俄罗斯站点已在南极洲运营——这是其挑战美国GPS主导地位的一部分努力，并且计划在像俄罗斯基地这样的地点设立新站点，位于圣三一东正教教堂的阴影下。

paragraphs.text: Elsewhere in Antarctica, Russian researchers boast of their recent discovery of a freshwater reserve the size of Lake Ontario after drilling through miles of solid ice. "You can see that we're here to stay," said Vladimir Cheberdak, 57, chief of the Bellingshausen Station, as he sipped tea under a portrait of Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen, a high-ranking officer in the Imperial Russian Navy who explored the Antarctic coast in 1820.
paragraphs.translation: 在南极洲其他地方，俄罗斯研究人员夸耀他们最近在钻穿数英里厚的坚冰后，发现了一个安大略湖大小的淡水储备。57岁的Bellingshausen站站长Vladimir Cheberdak说：“你可以看到我们是要留在这里的，”他一边喝茶，一边坐在Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen的肖像下，后者是帝国俄罗斯海军的高级军官，于1820年探索了南极海岸。

paragraphs.text: Antarctica's mineral, oil and gas wealth are a longer-term prize. The treaty banning mining here, shielding coveted (令人垂诞的) reserves of iron ore, coal and chromium, comes up for review in 2048. Researchers recently found kimberlite (金伯利岩) deposits hinting at the existence of diamonds. And while assessments vary widely, geologists estimate that Antarctica holds at least 36 billion barrels of oil and natural gas.
paragraphs.translation: 南极洲的矿产、石油和天然气财富是更长远的奖赏。禁止在这里采矿的条约，保护着令人垂涎的铁矿石、煤炭和铬矿储备，将于2048年接受审查。研究人员最近发现了金伯利岩矿床，暗示存在钻石。尽管评估差异很大，地质学家估计南极洲至少拥有360亿桶石油和天然气。

paragraphs.text: Beyond the Antarctic treaties, huge obstacles persist to tapping these resources, like drifting icebergs that could jeopardize offshore platforms. Then there is Antarctic's remoteness. with some mineral deposits found in windswept locations on a continent that is larger than Europe and where winter temperatures hover around minus 55 degrees Celsius.
paragraphs.translation: 除了南极条约，开采这些资源还存在巨大障碍，如漂移的冰山可能危及海上平台。还有南极洲的偏远。一些矿床位于风蚀地点，这个大陆比欧洲还大，冬季温度徘徊在零下55摄氏度左右。

paragraphs.text: But advances in technology might make Antarctica a lot more accessible three decades from now. And even before then, scholars warn, the demand for resources in an energy-hungry world could raise pressure to renegotiate Antarctica's treaties, possibly allowing more commercial endeavours here well before the prohibitions against them expire. The research stations on King George Island offer a glimpse into the long game on this ice-blanketed continent as nations assert themselves, eroding the sway long held by countries like the United States, Britain, Australia and New Zealand.
paragraphs.translation: 但技术进步可能使南极洲在三十年后变得更容易接近。学者们警告说，甚至在此之前，能源饥渴的世界对资源的需求可能增加重新谈判南极条约的压力，可能允许更多商业活动在禁令到期前在这里进行。乔治王岛上的研究站提供了一个窗口，可以看到各国在这个冰雪覆盖的大陆上的长期博弈，它们正在削弱美国、英国、澳大利亚和新西兰等国家长期保持的影响力。

paragraphs.text: Being stationed in Antarctica involves adapting to life on the planet's driest, windiest and coldest continent, yet each nation manages to make itself at home. Bearded Russian priests offer regular services at the Orthodox church for the 16 or so Russian speakers who spend the winter at the base, largely polar scientists in fields like glaciology and meteorology. Their number climbs to about 40 in the warmer summer months. China has arguably the fastest-growing operations in Antarctica. It opened its fourth station last year and is pressing ahead with plans to build a fifth. It is building its second ice-breaking ship and setting up research drilling operations on an ice dome 13,422 feet above sea level that is one the planet's coldest places. Chinese officials say the expansion in Antarctica prioritises scientific research, but they also acknowledge that concerns about resource security" influence their moves.
paragraphs.translation: 驻扎在南极洲需要适应地球上最干燥、最多风和最寒冷大陆的生活，但每个国家都设法使自己感到舒适。留着胡子的俄罗斯牧师在东正教堂为大约16名在基地过冬的俄罗斯人提供定期服务，主要是冰川学和气象学等领域的极地科学家。在更温暖的夏季，他们的数量增加到约40人。可以说中国在南极洲的操作增长最快。去年它开放了第四个站点，并正推进建造第五个站点的计划。它正在建造第二艘破冰船，并在海拔13,422英尺的冰穹上设立研究钻探作业，这是地球上最冷的地方之一。中国官员说，在南极洲的扩张优先考虑科学研究，但他们也承认资源安全关切影响了他们的行动。

paragraphs.text: China's newly renovated Great Wall Station on King George Island makes the Russian and Chilean bases here seem outdated. "We do weather monitoring here and other research." Ning Xu, 53, the chief of the Chinese base, said over tea during a fierce blizzard (暴风雪) in late November. The large base he leads resembles a snowed-in college campus on holiday break, with the capacity to sleep more than 10 times the 13 people who were staying on through the Antarctic winter. Yong Yu, a Chinese microbiologist, showed off the spacious building, with empty desks under an illustrated timeline detailing the rapid growth of China's Antarctic operations since the 1980s. "We now feel equipped to grow," he said.
paragraphs.translation: 中国新近翻新的长城站使这里的俄罗斯和智利基地显得过时。中国基地站长、53岁的宁旭在11月底一场猛烈的暴风雪期间边喝茶边说：“我们在这里进行天气监测和其他研究。”他领导的大型基地像一个被大雪封住的校园在假期，其睡眠容量超过在南极洲过冬的13人10倍以上。中国微生物学家Yong Yu展示了这座宽敞的建筑，空桌子上方有一幅插图时间线，详细介绍了自20世纪80年代以来中国南极操作的快速发展。他说：“我们现在感到有能力增长。”

paragraphs.text: As some countries expand operations in Antarctica, the United States maintains three year-round stations on the continent with more than 1, 000 people during the southern hemisphere's summer, including those at the Amundsen-Scott station, built in 1956 at an elevation of 9,301 feet on a plateau at the South Pole. But US researchers quietly complain about budget restraints and having far fewer icebreakers the Russia, limiting the reach of the United States in Antarctica.
paragraphs.translation: 随着一些国家扩大在南极洲的操作，美国在该大陆维持三个全年站点，在南半球的夏季有超过1,000人，包括在阿蒙森-斯科特站的人员，该站建于1956年，位于南极高原海拔9,301英尺处。但美国研究人员私下抱怨预算限制和破冰船数量远少于俄罗斯，限制了美国在南极洲的影响力。

paragraphs.text: Scholars warn that Antarctica's political drift could blur the distinction between military and civilian activities long before the continent's treaties come up for renegotiation, especially in parts of Antarctica that are ideal for intercepting (拦截) signals from satellites or retasking satellite systems, potentially enhancing global electronic intelligence operations.
paragraphs.translation: 学者们警告说，南极洲的政治漂移可能早在大陆条约重新谈判之前就模糊军事和民用活动之间的区别，特别是在南极洲一些理想用于拦截卫星信号或重新部署卫星系统的部分，可能增强全球电子情报操作。

paragraphs.text: Some countries have had a hard time here, Brazil opened a research station in 1984, but it was largely destroyed by a fire that killed two members of the navy in 2012, the same year that a diesel-laden Brazilian barge sank near the base. As if that were not enough, a Brazilian C-130 Hercules military transport plane has remained stranded near the runway of Chile's air base here since it crash-landed in 2014.
paragraphs.translation: 一些国家在这里遭遇了困难，巴西于1984年开放了一个研究站，但在2012年被一场火灾基本摧毁，造成两名海军成员死亡，同年一艘载有柴油的巴西驳船在基地附近沉没。仿佛这还不够，一架巴西C-130大力神军用运输机自2014年坠毁后一直滞留在智利空军基地的跑道附近。

paragraphs.text: However, Brazil's stretch of misfortune has created opportunities for China, with a Chinese company winning the $100 million contract in 2015 to rebuild the Brazilian station.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，巴西的一连串不幸为中国创造了机会，一家中国公司在2015年赢得了价值1亿美元的合同来重建巴西站点。

paragraphs.text: Amid all the changes, Antarctica maintains its allure. South Korea opened its second Antarctic research base in 2014, describing it as a way to test robots developed by Korean researchers for use in extreme conditions. With Russia's help, Belarus is preparing to build its first Antarctic base. Colombia said this year that it planned to join other South American nations with bases in Antarctica.
paragraphs.translation: 在所有这些变化中，南极洲保持其吸引力。韩国于2014年开放了第二个南极研究基地，将其描述为测试韩国研究人员开发的用于极端条件下的机器人的方法。在俄罗斯的帮助下，白俄罗斯正准备建造其第一个南极基地。哥伦比亚今年表示计划加入其他在南极洲有基地的南美国家。

paragraphs.text: "The old days of the Antarctic being dominated by the interests and wishes of white men from European, Australasian and North American states are over," Said Klaus Dodds, a politics scholar at the University of London who specialises in Antarctica. "The reality is that Antarctica is geopolitically contested.
paragraphs.translation: “南极洲由来自欧洲、澳大利亚和北美国家的白人的利益和愿望主导的旧时代已经结束，”专门研究南极洲的伦敦大学政治学者Klaus Dodds说。“现实是，南极洲在地缘政治上是有争议的。”

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: According to Chinese officials, their activities in Antarctica lay greater emphasis on scientific research.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落J。段落J中提到'Chinese officials say the expansion in Antarctica prioritises scientific research'，这与陈述中的'their activities in Antarctica lay greater emphasis on scientific research'相对应。关键词匹配：emphasis on scientific research对应prioritises scientific research。

questions.statementText: Efforts to create one of the world's largest ocean sanctuaries failed because of Russia's obstruction.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落C。段落C中提到'Russia recently frustrated efforts to create one of the world's largest ocean sanctuaries here'，这与陈述中的'Efforts to create one of the world's largest ocean sanctuaries failed because of Russia's obstruction'相对应。关键词匹配：efforts to create对应create，Russia's obstruction对应frustrated efforts。

questions.statementText: With several monitoring stations operating in Antarctica, Russia is trying hard to counter America's dominance in the field of worldwide navigational facilities.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落E。段落E中提到'Russia is expanding its monitoring stations for Glonass, its version of the Global Positioning System (GPS)'和'part of its effort to challenge the dominance of the American GPS'，这与陈述中的'Russia is trying hard to counter America's dominance in the field of worldwide navigational facilities'相对应。关键词匹配：counter dominance对应challenge the dominance，worldwide navigational facilities对应Global Positioning System/GPS。

questions.statementText: According to geologists' estimates, Antarctica has enormous reserves of oil and natural gas.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落G。段落G中提到'geologists estimate that Antarctica holds at least 36 billion barrels of oil and natural gas'，这与陈述中的'Antarctica has enormous reserves of oil and natural gas'相对应。关键词匹配：enormous reserves对应holds at least 36 billion barrels。

questions.statementText: It is estimated that Antarctica boasts of the richest reserves of fresh water on earth.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'Antarctica is estimated to have the biggest reserves of fresh water on the planet'，这与陈述中的'It is estimated that Antarctica boasts of the richest reserves of fresh water on earth'相对应。关键词匹配：biggest reserves对应richest reserves，fresh water对应fresh water on earth。

questions.statementText: The demand for energy resources may compel renegotiation of Antarctica's treaties before their expiration.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落I。段落I中提到'the demand for resources in an energy-hungry world could raise pressure to renegotiate Antarctica's treaties'，这与陈述中的'The demand for energy resources may compel renegotiation of Antarctica's treaties before their expiration'相对应。关键词匹配：demand for resources对应demand for energy resources，renegotiate treaties对应compel renegotiation of treaties。

questions.statementText: Many countries are racing against each other to increase their business and strategic influence on Antarctica.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落B。段落B中提到'an array of countries are rushing to assert greater influence here'和'with an eye not just towards the day those protective treaties expire, but also for the strategic and commercial opportunities'，这与陈述中的'Many countries are racing against each other to increase their business and strategic influence on Antarctica'相对应。关键词匹配：rushing to assert greater influence对应racing to increase their influence，strategic and commercial opportunities对应business and strategic influence。

questions.statementText: Antarctica's harsh natural conditions constitute huge obstacles to the exploitation of its resources.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落H。段落H中提到'huge obstacles persist to tapping these resources'和'Antarctic's remoteness'以及'winter temperatures hover around minus 55 degrees Celsius'，这与陈述中的'Antarctica's harsh natural conditions constitute huge obstacles to the exploitation of its resources'相对应。关键词匹配：huge obstacles对应huge obstacles，harsh natural conditions对应remoteness和extreme temperatures。

questions.statementText: With competition from many countries, Antarctica is no longer dominated by the traditional white nations.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落Q。段落Q中提到'The old days of the Antarctic being dominated by the interests and wishes of white men from European, Australasian and North American states are over'，这与陈述中的'With competition from many countries, Antarctica is no longer dominated by the traditional white nations'相对应。关键词匹配：dominated by the interests and wishes of white men对应dominated by the traditional white nations。

questions.statementText: American scientists complain about lack of sufficient money and equipment for their expansion in Antarctica.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落L。段落L中提到'US researchers quietly complain about budget restraints and having far fewer icebreakers the Russia'，这与陈述中的'American scientists complain about lack of sufficient money and equipment for their expansion in Antarctica'相对应。关键词匹配：complain about budget restraints对应complain about lack of sufficient money，having far fewer icebreakers对应lack of equipment。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Any veteran nicotine addict will testify that fancy packaging plays no role in the decision to keep smoking. So, it is argued, stripping cartons of their branding will trigger no mass movement to quit.
paragraphs.translation: 任何资深的尼古丁成瘾者都会证明，花哨的包装在决定继续吸烟方面不起作用。因此，有人认为，剥离烟盒的品牌标识不会引发大规模戒烟运动。

paragraphs.text: But that isn't why the government — under pressure from cancer charities, health workers and the Labour party — has agreed to legislate for standardised packaging. The theory is that smoking should be stripped of any appeal to discourage new generations from starting in the first place. Plain packaging would be another step in the reclassification of cigarettes from inviting consumer products to narcotics (麻醉剂).
paragraphs.translation: 但这并不是政府——在癌症慈善机构、卫生工作者和工党的压力下——同意立法推行标准化包装的原因。其理论是，吸烟应被剥离任何吸引力，以阻止新一代人开始吸烟。朴素包装将是将香烟从诱人的消费品重新归类为麻醉剂的又一步。

paragraphs.text: Naturally, the tobacco industry is violently opposed. No business likes to admit that it sells addictive poison as a lifestyle choice. That is why government has historically intervened, banning advertising, imposing health warnings and punitive (惩罚性的) duties. This approach has led over time to a fall in smoking with numbers having roughly halved since the 1970s.
paragraphs.translation: 自然，烟草行业强烈反对。没有企业喜欢承认它销售成瘾毒药作为生活方式选择。这就是为什么政府历史上进行干预，禁止广告、施加健康警告和惩罚性关税。随着时间的推移，这种方法导致吸烟率下降，自20世纪70年代以来数字大致减半。

paragraphs.text: Evidence from Australia suggests plain packaging pushes society further along that road. Since tobacco is one of the biggest causes of premature death in the UK, a measure that tames the habit even by a fraction is worth trying.
paragraphs.translation: 来自澳大利亚的证据表明，朴素包装推动社会沿着那条路走得更远。由于烟草是英国过早死亡的最大原因之一，即使是稍微驯服这种习惯的措施也值得一试。

paragraphs.text: So why has it taken so long? The Department of Health declared its intention to consider the move in November 2010 and consulted through 2012. But the plan was suspended in July 2013. It did not escape notice that a lobbying firm set up by Lynton Crosby, David Cameron's election campaign director, had previously acted for Philip Morris International, (The prime minister denied there was a connection between his new adviser's outside interests and the change in legislative programme.) In November 2013, after an unnecessary round of additional consultation, health minister Jane Ellison said the government was minded to proceed after all. Now we are told Members of Parliament (MPs) will have a free vote before parliament is dissolved in March.
paragraphs.translation: 那么为什么花了这么长时间？卫生部在2010年11月宣布考虑这一举措，并在2012年进行了磋商。但该计划在2013年7月被暂停。值得注意的是，由戴维·卡梅伦的竞选活动总监林顿·克罗斯比设立的游说公司此前曾为菲利普·莫里斯国际公司服务。（首相否认他的新顾问的外部利益与立法计划的变化之间存在联系。）2013年11月，在不必要的一轮额外磋商后，卫生部长简·埃利森表示政府终究打算继续推进。现在我们被告知，议会解散前，国会议员将在3月进行自由投票。

paragraphs.text: Parliament has in fact already authorised the government to tame the tobacco trade. MPs voted overwhelmingly in favour of Labour amendments to the children and families bill last February that included the power to regulate for plain packaging. With sufficient will in Downing Street this would have been done already. But strength of will is the missing ingredient where Mr. Cameron and public health are concerned. His attitude to state intervention has looked confused ever since his bizarre 2006 lament (叹惜) that chocolate oranges placed seductively at supermarket check-outs fueled obesity.
paragraphs.translation: 事实上，议会已经授权政府驯服烟草贸易。国会议员在去年二月以压倒性多数投票支持工党对《儿童和家庭法案》的修正案，其中包括监管朴素包装的权力。如果唐宁街有足够的意志力，这早已完成。但在涉及卡梅伦先生和公共卫生时，意志力是缺失的要素。他对国家干预的态度自2006年他奇怪地哀叹超市收银台处诱人放置的巧克力橘子助长肥胖以来，一直显得困惑。

paragraphs.text: The government has moved reluctantly into a sensible public health policy, but with such obvious over-cautiousness that any political credit due belongs to the opposition. Without sustained external pressure it seems certain Mr. Cameron would still be hooked on the interests of big tobacco companies.
paragraphs.translation: 政府不情愿地转向了明智的公共卫生政策，但如此明显的过度谨慎使得任何应得的政治功劳都归于反对派。如果没有持续的外部压力，卡梅伦先生似乎仍然沉迷于大烟草公司的利益。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What do chain smokers think of cigarette packaging?

options.label: A
options.text: Fancy packaging can help to engage new smokers.

options.label: B
options.text: It has little to do with the quality or taste of cigarettes.

options.label: C
options.text: Plain packaging discourages non-smokers from taking up smoking.

options.label: D
options.text: It has little impact on their decision whether or not to quit smoking.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段中的描述，'Any veteran nicotine addict will testify that fancy packaging plays no role in the decision to keep smoking'，表明老烟民认为香烟包装对于他们是否继续吸烟几乎没有影响，因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到精美包装有助于吸引新烟民。
wrongOptions.B: 虽然提到了包装与香烟的质量或口味无关，但这并非老烟民的观点。
wrongOptions.C: 文章中没有提及普通包装对非吸烟者的影响。

questions.questionText: What has the UK government agreed to do concerning tobacco packaging?

options.label: A
options.text: Pass a law to standardise cigarette packaging.

options.label: B
options.text: Rid cigarette cartons of all advertisements.

options.label: C
options.text: Subsidise companies to adopt plain packaging.

options.label: D
options.text: Reclassify cigarettes according to packaging.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第二段提到，'The government...has agreed to legislate for standardised packaging'，即政府同意通过立法来标准化香烟包装，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 文章中提到禁止广告，但并未提及去除所有广告。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到政府资助公司采用普通包装。
wrongOptions.D: 文章中提到将香烟从诱人消费品重新分类为麻醉剂，但并未提及根据包装重新分类香烟。

questions.questionText: What has happened in Australia where plain packaging is implemented?

options.label: A
options.text: Premature death rates resulting from smoking have declined.

options.label: B
options.text: The number of smokers has dropped more sharply than in the UK.

options.label: C
options.text: The sales of tobacco substitutes have increased considerably.

options.label: D
options.text: Cigarette sales have been falling far more quickly than in the UK.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段指出英国吸烟人数自20世纪70年代以来大致减半（'a fall in smoking with numbers having roughly halved since the 1970s'），第四段紧接着说'Evidence from Australia suggests plain packaging pushes society further along that road'，即朴素包装让（澳大利亚）社会在吸烟人数下降这条路上走得比英国更远，对应选项B'The number of smokers has dropped more sharply than in the UK'。A项把英国的'过早死亡'误植到澳大利亚且文中并未说死亡率下降，属过度推断。故正确答案是B。

wrongOptions.A: 文中'过早死亡'是针对英国而言，并未说澳大利亚因吸烟导致的死亡率下降，属过度推断。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到烟草替代品的销售增加。
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到澳大利亚的香烟销售下降速度与英国的比较，比较的是吸烟人数而非销量。

questions.questionText: Why has it taken so long for the UK government to consider plain packaging?

options.label: A
options.text: Prime Minister Cameron has been reluctant to take action.

options.label: B
options.text: There is strong opposition from veteran nicotine addicts.

options.label: C
options.text: Many Members of Parliament are addicted to smoking.

options.label: D
options.text: Pressure from tobacco manufacturers remains strong.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到，'But strength of will is the missing ingredient where Mr. Cameron and public health are concerned'，表明卡梅伦在公共卫生问题上缺乏决心，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到老烟民对普通包装的强烈反对。
wrongOptions.C: 文章没有提到许多议员吸烟成瘾。
wrongOptions.D: 文章提到烟草制造商的压力，但并未将其作为英国政府考虑普通包装耗时较长的原因。

questions.questionText: What did Cameron say about chocolate oranges at supermarket checkouts?

options.label: A
options.text: They fueled a lot of controversy.

options.label: B
options.text: They attracted a lot of smokers.

options.label: C
options.text: They made more British people obese.

options.label: D
options.text: They had certain ingredients missing.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章倒数第二段提到卡梅伦在2006年曾表示，'chocolate oranges placed seductively at supermarket check-outs fueled obesity'，即他认为超市结账处诱人的巧克力橙子助长了肥胖问题，因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 文章没有提到巧克力橙子引发很多争议。
wrongOptions.B: 文章没有提到巧克力橙子吸引很多吸烟者。
wrongOptions.D: 文章没有提到巧克力橙子缺少某些成分。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: What a waste of money! In return for an average of £44,000 of debt, students get an average of only 14 hours of lecture and tutorial time a week in Britain. Annual fees have risen from £1,000 to £9,000 in the last decade, but contact time at university has barely risen at all. And graduating doesn't even provide any guarantee of a decent job; six in ten graduates today are in non-graduate jobs.
paragraphs.translation: 多么浪费钱！在英国，学生平均负债4.4万英镑，换来的却是每周平均仅14小时的讲座和辅导时间。过去十年间，学费从1000英镑涨至9000英镑，但大学的接触时间几乎没有增加。而且，毕业甚至不能保证找到体面的工作；如今十分之六的毕业生从事的是不需要大学学历的工作。

paragraphs.text: No wonder it has become fashionable to denounce many universities as little more than elaborate con-tricks (耳扇术). There's a lot for students to complain about; the repayment threshold for paying back loans will be frozen for five years, meaning that lower-paid graduates have to start repaying their loans ; and maintenance grants have been replaced by loans, meaning that students from poorer backgrounds face higher debt than those with wealthier parents.
paragraphs.translation: 难怪将许多大学贬低为不过是精心设计的骗局（耳扇术）已成为一种流行观点。学生有很多可抱怨之处：贷款的还款门槛将被冻结五年，这意味着收入较低的毕业生必须开始偿还贷款；生活补助金已被贷款取代，这意味着家境较差的学生将比父母更富裕的学生面临更高的债务。

paragraphs.text: Yet it still pays to go to university. If going to university doesn't work out, students pay very little — if any — of their tuition fees back; you only start repaying when you are earning £21,000 a year. Almost half of graduates — those who go on to earn less — will have a portion of their debt written off. It's not just the lectures and tutorials that are important. Education is the sum of what students teach each other in between lectures and seminars. Students do not merely benefit while at university; studies show they go on to be healthier and happier than non-graduates, and also far more likely to vote.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，上大学仍然值得。如果大学经历不顺利，学生只需偿还很少甚至无需偿还学费；只有在年收入达到2.1万英镑时才开始还款。近一半的毕业生——那些后续收入较低的人——将有一部分债务被免除。重要的不仅仅是讲座和辅导课。教育是学生在讲座和研讨会之间相互教导的总和。学生不仅在大学期间受益；研究表明，他们比非毕业生更健康、更快乐，而且更有可能参与投票。

paragraphs.text: Whatever your talents, it is extraordinarily difficult to get a leading job in most fields without having been to university. Recruiters circle elite universities like vultures (兀鹰). Many top firms will not even look at applications from those who lack a 2.1, i.e., an upper-second class degree, from an elite university. Students at university also meet those likely to be in leading jobs in the future, forming contacts for life. This might not be right, but school-leavers who fail to acknowledge as much risk making the wrong decision about going to university.
paragraphs.translation: 无论你有何才能，没有上过大学，在大多数领域都极难获得顶尖工作。招聘人员像秃鹫一样在精英大学周围盘旋。许多顶级公司甚至不会考虑没有来自精英大学2:1学位（即二等一级学位）的申请。大学生也会遇到那些未来可能身居要职的人，从而建立终身的人脉关系。这或许并不合理，但未能认识到这一点的离校生，可能在上大学的决定上犯错。

paragraphs.text: Perhaps the reason why so many universities offer their students so little is they know studying at a top university remains a brilliant investment even if you don't learn anything. Studying at university will only become less attractive if employers shift their focus away from where someone went to university — and there is no sign of that happening anytime soon. School-leavers may moan, but they have little choice but to embrace university and the student debt that comes with it.
paragraphs.translation: 或许，如此多的大学向学生提供的东西如此之少，原因在于他们知道，在顶尖大学学习即使学不到任何东西，仍然是一项明智的投资。只有当雇主将关注点从某人上过哪所大学转移开时，上大学才会变得不那么有吸引力——而短期内看不到任何这种迹象。离校生可能会抱怨，但他们别无选择，只能接受大学以及随之而来的学生债务。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What is the author's opinion of going to university?

options.label: A
options.text: It is worthwhile after all.

options.label: B
options.text: It is simply a waste of time.

options.label: C
options.text: It is hard to say whether it is good or bad.

options.label: D
options.text: It is too expensive for most young people.

questions.analysis: 这是一道观点态度题。文章最后一段提到'Perhaps the reason why so many universities offer their students so little is they know studying at a top university remains a brilliant investment even if you don't learn anything'，表明作者认为上大学是一项值得的投资。同时，文章也提到了上大学的诸多好处，如'studies show they go on to be healthier and happier than non-graduates'，'far more likely to vote'，'forming contacts for life'等，进一步印证了作者的正面态度。

wrongOptions.B: 'It is simply a waste of time'与作者观点相悖，文章明确表示上大学是值得的。
wrongOptions.C: 'It is hard to say whether it is good or bad'过于模棱两可，文章对上大学持肯定态度。
wrongOptions.D: 'It is too expensive for most young people'只关注了费用问题，忽略了作者强调的上大学的长期收益。

questions.questionText: What does the author say about the employment situation of British university graduates?

options.label: A
options.text: Few of them are satisfied with the jobs they are offered.

options.label: B
options.text: It usually takes a long time for them to find a decent job.

options.label: C
options.text: Graduates from elite universities usually can get decent jobs.

options.label: D
options.text: Most of them take jobs which don't require a college degree.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第一段提到'six in ten graduates today are in non-graduate jobs'，即60%的大学毕业生从事的是非大学毕业即可从事的工作，说明大多数毕业生从事的工作并不需要大学学位。

wrongOptions.A: 'Few of them are satisfied with the jobs they are offered'原文未提及毕业生对工作的满意度。
wrongOptions.B: 'It usually takes a long time for them to find a decent job'原文未提及找工作所需时间。
wrongOptions.C: 'Graduates from elite universities usually can get decent jobs'原文未提及名校毕业生的就业情况。

questions.questionText: What does the author say is important for university students besides classroom instruction?

options.label: A
options.text: Making sure to obtain an upper-second class degree.

options.label: B
options.text: Practical skills they will need in their future careers.

options.label: C
options.text: Interactions among themselves outside the classroom.

options.label: D
options.text: Developing independent and creative thinking abilities.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段提到'Education is the sum of what students teach each other in between lectures and seminars'，强调了学生在课堂之外的互动对他们的教育同样重要。

wrongOptions.A: 'Making sure to obtain an upper-second class degree'只是大学学习的一个方面，并非作者强调的重点。
wrongOptions.B: 'Practical skills they will need in their future careers'原文未提及。
wrongOptions.D: 'Developing independent and creative thinking abilities'原文未提及。

questions.questionText: What is said to be an advantage of going to university?

options.label: A
options.text: Learning how to take risks in an ever-changing world.

options.label: B
options.text: Meeting people who will be helpful to you in the future.

options.label: C
options.text: Having opportunities of playing a leading role in society.

options.label: D
options.text: Gaining up-to-date knowledge in science and technology.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第四段提到'Students at university also meet those likely to be in leading jobs in the future, forming contacts for life'，说明在大学期间结识未来可能在重要职位的人，对个人未来发展有帮助。

wrongOptions.A: 'Learning how to take risks in an ever-changing world'原文未提及。
wrongOptions.C: 'Having opportunities of playing a leading role in society'并非上大学的直接优势。
wrongOptions.D: 'Gaining up-to-date knowledge in science and technology'原文未提及。

questions.questionText: What can we infer from the last paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: It is natural for students to make complaints about university education.

options.label: B
options.text: Few students are willing to bear the burden of debt incurred at university.

options.label: C
options.text: University education is becoming attractive to students who can afford it.

options.label: D
options.text: The prestige of the university influences employers' recruitment decisions.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到'Studying at university will only become less attractive if employers shift their focus away from where someone went to university — and there is no sign of that happening anytime soon'，说明雇主对大学背景的重视是大学教育吸引力的关键因素。

wrongOptions.A: 'It is natural for students to make complaints about university education'原文未提及学生抱怨的自然性。
wrongOptions.B: 'Few students are willing to bear the burden of debt incurred at university'与原文意思相反，原文提到学生别无选择。
wrongOptions.C: 'University education is becoming attractive to students who can afford it'原文未提及教育费用与吸引力的关系。

questionGroups.sourceText: 随着中国经济的蓬勃发展，学汉语的人数迅速增加，使汉语成了世界上人们最爱学的语言之一。近年来，中国大学在国际上的排名也有了明显的提高。由于中国教育的巨大进步，中国成为最受海外学生欢迎的留学目的地之一就不足为奇了。2015年，近四十万国际学生蜂拥来到中国学习。他们学习的科目不再限于中国语言和文化，而包括科学与工程。在全球教育市场上，美国和英国仍占主导地位，但中国正在迅速赶上。

answer.modelTranslation: With the vigorous development of China's economy, the number of people learning Chinese has increased rapidly, making Chinese one of the most popular languages in the world to learn. In recent years, the international rankings of Chinese universities have also seen a significant improvement. It is no surprise that China has become one of the most popular destinations for overseas students due to the tremendous progress in Chinese education. In 2015, nearly 400,000 international students flocked to China to study. Their subjects of study are no longer limited to Chinese language and culture, but include science and engineering as well. Although the United States and the United Kingdom still dominate the global education market, China is catching up rapidly.
translationNotes: 注意'随着'的翻译，可用with或as引导
'使...成了...'译为making...one of...，注意使用现在分词作结果状语
'近年来'译为in recent years，表示从过去到现在的一段时间
'由于...'译为due to...，注意使用介词短语作原因状语
'就不足为奇了'译为it is no surprise that...，注意使用形式主语句型
注意'蜂拥来到'的翻译，可用flocked to...，注意使用过去时态
'不再限于...而包括...'译为are no longer limited to...but include...，注意使用并列连词but
注意'虽然...但...'的翻译，可用Although...but...，注意使用让步状语从句
